tasks.short: Advise the project team and sign the advice note

steps.what: Ask the premarket, export, labeling or clinical question
Return accepted records for that topic
Draft the advice note from those records

loop.input: accepted records and the advice template
loop.output: note that cites rule record ids only
loop.check: Every cited id is on the advice source list
loop.stop: Leave the point blank and stop if no record id supports it
loop.why_not_simpler: The advice sentence is not a fixed reply stored on the topic

steps.what: Sign the advice note
Talk the team through the signed note
Note what the team will change

tasks.design: The project lead asks with product id, market and a topic of premarket, export, labeling or clinical study compliance, on a {WORKFLOW} form. An answer view returns accepted rule records from {DOCS}. A note may cite only those records. The specialist signs it, then talks the team through the dispute. The meeting is not replaced. Nothing is sent to {GOV_PORTAL}. The old thread in {EMAIL} is not the record.
tasks.previous_blocker: Advice was given in meetings and mail with no record of which rule the answer used.
tasks.enabler_now: A question can name a topic and a market, and accepted records can be cited by id.
tasks.still_hard: Whether the rule fits this study or this label is a judgement, and the team conversation does not become a form.
tasks.human_edge: The specialist signs the advice and decides what to say when the team disputes it.

ambition.what: Sign an advice note in the week the question is asked, and meet only when the note is disputed

tasks.altitude: Searching for the rule shrinks. The specialist still signs the note and still holds the meeting when the team needs to argue it.

reach.task: Change the plan only where the signed advice note requires it
reach.learn: Which topics already have a signed note and which questions are still open

evidence.claim: Advising a project team is a conversation plus a written note. The note can be drafted from accepted records. The meeting stays, because the hard part is the judgement and the people in the room.
Digest [S27] says a consultancy partly refunded a government report after a model cited sources that did not exist, so the advice note may cite only accepted rule record ids.

assumptions: Focal role is the regulatory affairs specialist. The task ends at the signed note and the meeting about it. It does not file a submission or approve a protocol.

Input contract: question id, product id, market, topic (premarket, export, labeling or clinical), rule record id. Producer of the question is the project lead. Producer of the records is the accepted knowledge base. A question with no topic returns no records. If the form is empty the specialist types the same fields from mail and marks the row manual.
Meetings are a real share of this task and stay. Test the native {DOCS} answer view and {WORKFLOW} form before any custom code.
unknowns: Which of the four topics the firm actually asks about.
Who may sign advice when the specialist is absent.
Whether clinical questions need a second reviewer.
research_questions: What share of advice questions match an accepted record?
How often does the meeting change the signed note?

already_counted.description: Specialist edits the advice note before signing
Meeting time on disputed points stays with the specialist

incremental.description: Add a topic label when questions use a word the form does not list
Project leads restate a question that had no topic

approvals.approved_version: advice note signed for this question id

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes questions arrive as unstructured mail, so the record lookup is empty and the specialist still prepares the note by hand. The high case assumes a clean topic but every note is signed and every disputed point is still discussed. The meeting is not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Interpret a rule change into a signed procedure

steps.what: Open a policy impact from the accepted rule
Draft the regulatory procedure delta from that rule

loop.input: accepted rule record and the current procedure
loop.output: delta that cites the rule record id
loop.check: Each changed clause cites that rule record id, and other clauses are marked unchanged
loop.stop: Leave a clause blank and stop if it would cite any other source
loop.why_not_simpler: The operational meaning of a clause is not a sentence stored on the rule record

steps.what: Comment on how the change hits operations
Sign the procedure version
Publish that signed procedure version
Notify owners of the new procedure version

tasks.design: When an accepted rule record changes, {WORKFLOW} opens an impact item with the rule record id and the policy id. A draft in {DOCS} proposes procedure edits only where the text must change, and marks other clauses unchanged. The quality reviewer comments on the operational effect. The specialist signs one procedure version. That version is published internally and owners are told. It is not sent to {GOV_PORTAL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Rule changes were interpreted in mail, and the procedure was rewritten in full, so readers could not see what had actually changed.
tasks.enabler_now: An accepted rule record has an id, so a clause can cite that id or be marked unchanged.
tasks.still_hard: What the rule requires of this firm, beyond the words on the page, is still a judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The specialist interprets the rule and signs the only procedure version that is published.

ambition.what: Issue a procedure delta in the same month as the accepted rule change, not at the annual review

tasks.altitude: Full rewrites shrink to deltas. The specialist can refuse a draft that cites no rule record, and can withhold publication.

reach.task: Comment on how the procedure change hits operations
reach.learn: Which procedure version is signed and which clauses were marked unchanged

evidence.claim: Turning a rule change into a corporate procedure is a delta plus a signature. The interpretation stays with the specialist. Publishing an unsigned rewrite would hide what changed.
Digest [S27] says a consultancy partly refunded a government report after a model cited sources that did not exist, so each changed clause must cite the accepted rule record and no other source.

assumptions: Focal role is the regulatory affairs specialist. The task ends when the signed procedure version is published internally. Training people on it is a separate task.

Input contract: rule record id, policy id, clause id, change flag. Producer of the rule record is the accepted knowledge base. Producer of the operational comment is the quality reviewer. A clause that cites no rule record id is not published. If there is no accepted record the specialist writes the impact by hand and marks it manual.
Test native {DOCS} templates, version history and {WORKFLOW} items before any custom code. The notice to owners uses the signed version id only, in a fixed sentence.
unknowns: Which policies map to which rule records.
Who may sign a procedure when the specialist is absent.
Whether some rule changes need a works process outside this task.
research_questions: What share of rule changes touch an existing procedure?
How often does the specialist reject the first delta?

already_counted.description: Specialist edits the delta before signing
Interpretation and signature stay with the specialist

incremental.description: Map a new rule record to the procedure it can change
Quality reviewers restate an operations comment the specialist rejected

approvals.approved_version: procedure version signed for this rule record id

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes rule changes are not yet accepted records, so the delta cannot cite an id and the specialist still rewrites the procedure by hand. The high case assumes a clean record but every interpretation is still signed. Training time is not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Review a report for rigor, accuracy and clarity

steps.what: Submit the report, the table and the claims
Flag numbers or claims that do not match

loop.input: table cells, report sentences and claim source ids
loop.output: mismatch list with cell or claim ids
loop.check: Each flag names a table cell and a sentence, or a claim id with no source id
loop.stop: One pass, then stop; do not rewrite the report
loop.why_not_simpler: A wording difference that is not the same number or a missing source id needs reading

steps.what: Sign the review of rigor, accuracy and clarity
Attach the signed review to the pack
Answer a finding on the source data

tasks.design: The project lead submits report id, data table id and a claim list into {WORKFLOW}. A bounded pass over the report in {DOCS} flags a number that disagrees between the table and the text, and a claim with no source id. It does not rewrite the science. The specialist signs a review of rigor, accuracy and clarity. Only that signed note is attached to the pack. The report is not filed to {GOV_PORTAL} in this task.
tasks.previous_blocker: Numbers were checked by eye across long reports, and a comment in mail did not name the cell it referred to.
tasks.enabler_now: A table cell and a sentence can be compared, and a claim can be required to carry a source id.
tasks.still_hard: Scientific rigor is not a mismatch flag. A consistent number can still be the wrong number.
tasks.human_edge: The specialist judges rigor, accuracy and clarity, and can refuse to let the report into the pack.

ambition.what: Return a signed review while the report is still in draft, not after the submission pack is built

tasks.altitude: Cross-checks of numbers and citations take less time. The specialist keeps the scientific judgement and the right to block the report.

reach.task: Answer a finding on the source data
reach.learn: Which findings are signed and which claims had no source id

evidence.claim: Technical review of a report is mostly reading. A comparison can flag a number that does not match or a claim with no source. It cannot decide that the science is sound.
Digest [S27] says a consultancy partly refunded a government report after a model cited sources that did not exist, so the check may only flag a missing source id. It does not judge the science.

assumptions: Focal role is the regulatory affairs specialist. The task ends when a signed review note is attached to the pack or the specialist refuses the report. Portal filing is a separate task.

Input contract: report id, table id, claim id, source id, cell reference. Producer is the project lead. A claim with no source id is flagged and not repaired by the check. If the report is a scan with no cell ids the specialist reviews it by hand and marks the row manual.
The model prior fits the mismatch flag only. The judgement step has no loop. Test native {DOCS} comparison and {WORKFLOW} fields before any custom code.
unknowns: Whether source tables have stable cell ids.
Who may sign a review when the specialist is absent.
Which reports are too unstructured for a cell comparison.
research_questions: What share of claims arrive with no source id?
How often does the specialist block a report whose numbers matched?

already_counted.description: Specialist checks a weak mismatch before the review
Rigor judgement stays with the specialist

incremental.description: Extend the mismatch check when a new table layout appears
Project leads add a source id the check flagged as missing

approvals.approved_version: review note signed for this report id

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes reports are scans without cell or source ids, so the flag rarely fires and the specialist still reads every page by hand. The high case assumes clean ids but the rigor judgement is still fully manual. Rewriting the report is not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Review a label, promo, batch, spec or method

steps.what: Submit the label, promo, batch, spec or method
Compare spec limits and required batch fields
List label or promo claims outside the accepted list

loop.input: label or promo text and the accepted claim list
loop.output: claims that are not on the list
loop.check: Each listed claim is a span in the artefact and is absent from the accepted claim list
loop.stop: One pass, then stop; do not rewrite the label or the promo text
loop.why_not_simpler: A claim can share words with an allowed claim and still not be that claim

steps.what: Sign the compliance finding
Read the finding before release of the batch

tasks.design: The product owner submits artefact type and version: promotional material, labeling, batch record, specification sheet or test method, with product id, on a {WORKFLOW} form. Coded spec limits, required batch fields and method ids are compared in {DOCS} to the signed master. A separate pass lists label or promo claims that are not on the accepted claim list. The specialist signs one compliance finding. A {SPREADSHEET} of comments is not the record. Nothing is sent to {GOV_PORTAL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Labels, batch records and specs were read as whole documents, so a changed limit and a new claim were easy to miss.
tasks.enabler_now: Limits and required fields can be compared as values, and a claim can be checked against an accepted list.
tasks.still_hard: A promotional claim can be on the list and still be presented in a misleading way. That reading stays with the specialist.
tasks.human_edge: The specialist signs the compliance finding and can block an artefact the comparison did not catch.

ambition.what: Sign a compliance finding on each new label, promo, batch, spec or method before it is used, not in a monthly pile

tasks.altitude: Coded comparisons shrink. The specialist still reads claims and signs the finding, and can stop an artefact that is numerically clean.

reach.task: Hold a batch or a method until the signed finding is in
reach.learn: Which artefact versions have a signed finding and which claims were outside the list

evidence.claim: Reviewing a label, a promo piece, a batch record, a spec or a test method splits in two. Coded limits and required fields can be compared. Promotional and label claims still need a person, because a matching word can be a misleading presentation.

Digest [S27] says a consultancy partly refunded a government report after a model cited sources that did not exist, so a finding may not treat a claim as allowed unless it is on the accepted claim list.

assumptions: Focal role is the regulatory affairs specialist. The task ends at the signed compliance finding. It does not approve the batch for release and it does not file a submission.

Input contract: artefact id, artefact type (promo, label, batch, spec or method), version, product id, limit name, limit value, method id, claim text. Producer is the product owner. A spec or method with no version is not compared. If the form is empty the specialist types the same fields and marks the row manual.

A test method is checked as a document id against the signed master, not rewritten. Test native {DOCS} comparison and the {WORKFLOW} form before any custom code. The claim pass does not rewrite the label.
unknowns: Whether batch records expose required fields as values.
Who may sign a finding when the specialist is absent.
Which claim list is the accepted one for each market.
research_questions: What share of label claims are absent from the accepted list?
How often does the specialist block an artefact whose limits matched?

already_counted.description: Specialist reads unlisted claims before the finding
Compliance judgement stays with the specialist

incremental.description: Add a required batch field or limit name when a master changes
Product owners correct an artefact version the compare could not read

approvals.approved_version: compliance finding signed for this artefact version

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes specs and batch records are still unstructured scans, so the value comparison rarely runs and the specialist still reads every page. The high case assumes coded limits but every claim reading and every finding is still signed. Batch release itself is not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Advice, procedure updates and compliance reviews still end with the specialist, but the week is no longer spent searching for the rule or comparing numbers by hand.
reach: Project leads receive a signed advice note before the meeting, and a signed review before a report enters a pack.
Quality reviewers see the compliance finding on a label, a batch, a spec or a method.
Product owners get a procedure version that names the rule record it came from.
skills_to_grow: Advise from accepted records, and keep the meeting for the dispute.
Write a procedure delta that shows what the rule change did and did not change.
Flag a number or a citation that does not match, and still judge the science.
Separate a coded limit check from a promotional claim that needs a reading.
role.ambitious_version: Each accepted rule change produces a signed procedure, and no label, promo piece, batch record, spec, method or report enters a pack without a signed finding.
